title: @Cacheable: The Java Annotation That Skips the DB
description:
Spring's @Cacheable annotation lets a Java service check an in-memory cache before ever touching the database -- and @CacheEvict keeps it from serving stale data after a write. Swap the cache provider to Redis and every replica of your service shares the same cache, with zero changes to the annotations themselves. This is one piece of the Java Mastery Path's guide to performance at scale, covering JVM tuning, HikariCP connection pools, and caching strategies.

Source lesson:
- https://sigilipelli.github.io/java-mastery-path/level-4/09-performance-at-scale/

#Shorts

beats.narration: Your Java service is hammering the database with the same query, over and over. One annotation fixes that -- no loops, no manual cache checks.
Add @Cacheable to findBySku, and Spring checks the cache first. Only a real cache miss ever touches the database -- every call after that returns instantly.
Update the price, and @CacheEvict clears the stale entry so nobody reads old data. Every replica of your service shares that same rule, even when the cache itself moves to Redis.
That's the whole trick -- swap one line in your properties file to point at Redis, and every instance shares the same cache. The annotations in your code never change.

display.heading: Same code, different backend
display.subheading: spring.cache.type=redis -- the @Cacheable/@CacheEvict annotations don't change at all
